summary.text: Nancy Wallace is the Green Party nominee for Maryland's 8th Congressional District and a federal-contract data coordinator with a background in environmental lobbying. She has run for office as a Green Party candidate several times, including for governor in 2022, and describes her campaign as focused on climate and economic transformation.

paragraphs.text: Wallace was born in Long Island, New York, in 1956 and raised in Bethesda, Maryland, according to her campaign website; she graduated from Walt Whitman High School.
She holds a bachelor's degree in political science from Yale University and, according to her campaign website, attended the University of Virginia law school for one year.

Wallace describes spending about 14 years lobbying Congress on international environmental issues, including founding the International Entanglement Network (1983-85) and serving as the Sierra Club's Washington Director for its International Population Program (1990-94).

From 1994 she says she worked as a federal information-technology contractor (Electronic Data Systems, later Computer Sciences Corporation) and later supported the Department of the Navy and Marine Corps; she currently supports the Department of Commerce as a data coordinator for ecological restoration projects.
Wallace joined the Green Party in 2003 and, according to her campaign website, has co-chaired the Montgomery County Green Party since February 2015.
She ran for U.S. House in Maryland's 8th District in 2016 and 2024 and was the Green nominee for governor in 2022, receiving 0.7%.
